solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Star with nothing left trapped in foreign capital

indicators.note: trapped in says the pieces before it sit inside the capital city that follows

parts.note: Paris is the capital of France, a foreign capital to a British solver
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A celebrity with no money left is stuck in some overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pole Star, the bright star near the celestial north pole, is known by this name.

clue.text: One against possible energy source? Shame!

parts.note: a con is an argument or person against, as in pros and cons
nuclear fusion is a hoped-for source of power, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: An opponent of some untested power scheme is exclaiming in disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: The older sense of the definition is embarrassment or disgrace, as in 'to my utter confusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: In older usage this word meant disgrace or abashment, as when someone is put to embarrassment.

clue.text: Quiet song conveys a religious code

parts.note: sh is the instruction to be quiet
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: A soft hymn carries the message of a faith's laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic law, derived from the Koran and tradition, is the code meant here.

clue.text: Thus paper company has sent out man to provide computer info

parts.note: so means thus or in this way
FT is the Financial Times, the British newspaper printed on pink paper

indicators.note: has sent out says the letters of the following word leave the word company

explanation.surface: A publishing firm sacks a man, and this gives a computing service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has sent out' removes M, A and N from COMPANY, leaving COPY.
explanation.definitionFit: A document held electronically rather than printed on paper is information on a computer.

clue.text: Unpremeditated fun with mother — spot me looking excited

indicators.note: looking excited suggests the letters of fun, mother and spot me are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A child sees their mum at an event and gets thrilled at the impromptu fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An action taken impulsively, without forethought, is done on the spur of the moment.

clue.text: Is child upset having tucked into inauthentic food item?

indicators.note: having tucked into says the jumbled letters go inside the word for inauthentic

parts.note: fake means not genuine

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the child abbreviation is read bottom to top

explanation.surface: A child is upset after eating something that isn't real food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks emotional but, in a down clue, turns the child abbreviation over, giving HC.
explanation.definitionFit: A patty of flaked fish and potato, often breadcrumbed, is a familiar thing to eat.

clue.text: Animal I found lying under garment

indicators.note: in a down clue, lying under places the letter I below the garment word

parts.note: a coat is an outer garment

explanation.surface: I discovered a creature sleeping beneath my coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-nosed raccoon relative from Central and South America is the creature meant.

clue.text: Quietly try again to call up rural slave

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to redial is to phone a number again after failing to get through

explanation.surface: Someone softly phoning back a farm labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to land or farms, this adjective describes a serf bound to work an estate.

clue.text: Malevolent god to move in desultory fashion across lake

indicators.note: across says the drifting verb stretches over the lake letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to mooch is to wander about aimlessly

explanation.surface: An evil deity drifts aimlessly over a body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canaanite deity to whom children were sacrificed, used for any cruel demanding power.

clue.text: Naughty nudes about to have a meal on the floor?

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the eating word
naughty suggests the letters of nudes behaving badly and getting rearranged

parts.note: to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: Rude naked diners about to picnic on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naughty' produces the arrangement UNSED; the question mark flags that the definition is a playful description of someone thrown from a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider thrown from the saddle, or a person tipped off a chair, ends up on the ground.

clue.text: Traveller in conflict around start of year given food

indicators.note: around says the conflict word encloses the next pieces

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of year

parts.note: fare is food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: A traveller caught in fighting is fed at the beginning of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone journeying on foot along the way is a traveller, especially in older writing.

clue.text: Judge top commander slowing down inside

indicators.note: inside says the slowing term goes within the commander abbreviation

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
rit, ritardando, is the musical direction for slowing down

explanation.surface: A judge notes a senior commander's slackening pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A reviewer who assesses and pronounces on the merit of work is a judge of it.

clue.text: Old officer to leave something behind for waiters?

definitions.meaning: a court official who carried a metal-tipped staff of office

definitions.text: to leave something behind for waiters?
definitions.meaning: read in two words, giving the serving employees a gratuity

explanation.surface: A former official departs, leaving a gratuity for the restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a court usher or bailiff carrying a staff, and cryptically a split phrase about gratuities.

clue.text: Fish ordered for Spooner? Get a grip!

indicators.note: for Spooner says swap the opening sounds of the two words, as the Reverend Spooner did

parts.note: hake is a sea fish
told means ordered, as in told to leave

explanation.surface: A diner orders fish and is told to pull themselves together.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize firmly or to become established, an idiom close to taking a grip on something.

clue.text: Henry sitting on stairs in the gloom?

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting on places the name above the stairs word

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as in Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a flight is a series of stairs

explanation.surface: Henry sits on the staircase in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dim light at dusk or dawn, neither bright nor dark, is a kind of gloom.

clue.text: Domestic situation? Take steps ahead of finding new team

indicators.note: in a down clue, ahead of puts the sacking word before the team word

parts.note: to fire is to sack, the disciplinary step taken against staff
a side is a team, here the one hired to replace the old

explanation.surface: A football manager acts decisively before signing a fresh squad.
explanation.walkthrough: You may have to sack the existing team before finding a new side.
explanation.definitionFit: The area round the hearth at home stands for cosy home life, a domestic setting.

clue.text: A bloke gets to eat a candle maybe!

parts.note: man means a bloke or chap
to dine is to eat a meal

explanation.surface: An absurd picture of a man chewing on a candle.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means flavoured with almonds; the blog takes the definition as an almond-scented candle, hence 'maybe!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means made or scented with almonds, so it could describe a scented candle.

clue.text: Sailor's friend, man with backward-looking wife

parts.note: a mate is a friend
in Genesis, Lot's wife looked back at Sodom and became a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: A seaman's pal is a man whose wife keeps looking back.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang word, from French, for a seaman.

clue.text: Torment base and wicked

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation, as a road bed
evil means wicked

explanation.surface: Cruelty that is low and wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To plague or harass persistently, as a devil might, is to torment.

clue.text: Changes ways whenever one needs to be accommodated

indicators.note: to be accommodated says the pieces are housed inside the ways word

parts.note: modes are ways or methods
if can mean whenever, as in if it rains we stay in
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone alters their habits whenever a guest needs putting up.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter or adjust something in part is to change it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Make off from city area bathed in mist?

indicators.note: bathed in says the city area is wrapped inside the mist word

parts.note: damp is moisture, as in a damp mist
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Fleeing a foggy part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave suddenly or secretly, as an army breaking camp, is to make off.

clue.text: Eastern term of respect engraved into nation's monument

indicators.note: engraved into says the title is cut inside the nation word, apt for a monument

parts.note: a state is a nation
U is a Burmese title of respect, as in U Thant

explanation.surface: An Oriental honorific is carved into a country's memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved or cast figure erected in memory of someone is a kind of monument.

clue.text: Available in Exmouth, a light meal at the Indian

indicators.note: Available in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A snack on offer at a Devon seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Exmouth is a seaside town in Devon; 'light' looks like it describes the meal but belongs to the hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection of small dishes on a round tray is a typical meal in an Indian restaurant.

clue.text: It's nuts crossing ravine, as one may get a stitch

definitions.text: as one may get a stitch

indicators.note: crossing says the crazy word spans the ravine, holding it within

parts.note: mad means crazy, nuts
a chine is a deep ravine, a word used on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset

explanation.surface: Someone thinks it madness to cross a gorge while suffering a sharp side pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stitch' suggests a pain in the side, but means sewing: what is sewn by machine is stitched.
explanation.definitionFit: Sewn by machine, as a seam gains its stitches when put through a sewing machine.

clue.text: Small portion at end of meadow has iron fence? It won't cause much bother

indicators.note: fence says the iron symbol encloses the other pieces

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: at end of places the small portion after the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
a bit is a small portion

explanation.surface: A corner of a field with iron railings, which is no great nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny insect bite, and figuratively a trifling nuisance hardly worth worrying about.

clue.text: Maiden's exclamation of surprise with atmosphere created by fabric

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
oh is a cry of surprise
air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A girl gasps at the mood a cloth creates.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or yarn made from the hair of the Angora goat is a fabric.

clue.text: Harsh voices finally coming against nuclear missile

indicators.note: coming against puts the letter right next to the missile word
finally picks the last letter of voices

parts.note: Trident is the British submarine-launched nuclear missile

explanation.surface: Shrill voices are finally raised against nuclear weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and grating in sound, like a shrill protest voice.
